members.name: shared
members.comment:
A shared singleton instance for accessing network slicing functionality.

Use this shared instance to access all network slicing capabilities.
The `CTSlicingManager` uses a singleton pattern to ensure consistent state management across your app.
```swift
let manager = CTSlicingManager.shared
```

declarations.name: CTSlicingManager.AppCategory
declarations.comment:
Application categories you use with network slicing.

Network slicing allows carriers to optimize their network for specific types of applications.
The `AppCategory` enum defines the supported application types that can use network slicing.
You can use a category only when all of the following conditions are met:
- The carrier's network supports the specific slice category. For example, a carrier may support communication slices but not gaming slices.
- Your app has the appropriate entitlements for that category.
- The device and network conditions allow network slicing.

Always check ``CTSlicingManager/availableSliceAppCategories`` before you attempt to activate a category. Availability depends on both carrier network support and your app's entitlements.

members.name: description
members.comment:
A string representation of the application category.

This property provides a string representation of the category, suitable for debugging and logging purposes.
> Important: This description isn't localized, so don't display it to people in your app's interface.
> For text that people see, provide your own localized strings based on the category value.

members.name: allCases
members.comment:
All application categories supported at the current OS version.

On iOS 26.3 and later, this property returns `[.gaming, .communication, .streaming]`.
On iOS 27.0 and later, this property also includes `.missionCritical`.

Use this property to enumerate all valid categories at runtime without checking the OS version directly.

declarations.name: CTSlicingManager.Slice
declarations.comment:
Information about an active network slice.

A `Slice` represents an active network slice configuration, including the app category it serves, the traffic class it uses, and the network interface handling the traffic.
Use the ``CTSlicingManager/activeSlices`` property to retrieve information about currently active slices on the device.

members.name: appCategory
members.comment:
An application category associated with this network slice.

This property identifies which type of application traffic the slice optimizes for, such as gaming, communication, or streaming.

members.name: trafficClass
members.comment:
A traffic class that routes traffic through this network slice.

The traffic class indicates the quality of service characteristics for the slice, such as voice, video, or background data.
When the network slice doesn't have a specific traffic class restriction, this property returns ``CTSlicingManager/TrafficClass/any``, indicating the slice can handle all types of network traffic.

members.name: networkInterfaceName
members.comment:
A network interface name associated with the slice.

This property contains the system name of the network interface that handles traffic for this network slice, such as "pdp_ip0".

declarations.name: CTSlicingManager.TrafficClass
declarations.comment:
Quality-of-service levels for network traffic routing.

The `TrafficClass` enum represents different quality of service (QoS) levels that the network uses to prioritize and route traffic.
Each traffic class has specific characteristics optimized for different types of network communication.
The system automatically assigns traffic classes based on the active network slice and the type of traffic being transmitted.

members.name: description
members.comment:
A string representation of the traffic class.

This property provides a string representation of the traffic class, suitable for debugging and logging purposes.
> Important: This description isn't localized, so don't display it to people in your app's interface.
> For text that people see, provide your own localized strings based on the traffic class value.

declarations.name: CTTelephonyNetworkInfo.RadioAccessTechnologyDidChangeMessage
declarations.comment:
A message that posts when the radio access technology changes for one of the services.

Use the ``serviceIdentifier`` property  as the key in ``CTTelephonyNetworkInfo/serviceCurrentRadioAccessTechnology`` to get the value of the new radio access technology for the service.

members.name: makeMessage
members.comment:
Converts a posted notification into this asynchronous message type for any observers.

To implement this method in your own `AsyncMessage` conformance, retrieve values from the ``Notification``'s ``Notification/userInfo`` and set them as properties on the message.
- Parameter notification: The posted ``Notification``.
- Returns: The converted `AsyncMessage`, or `nil` if conversion is not possible.

members.name: makeNotification
members.comment:
Converts a posted asynchronous message into a notification for any observers.

To implement this method in your own `AsyncMessage` conformance, use the properties defined by the message to populate the ``Notification``'s ``Notification/userInfo``.
- Parameters:

- Returns: The converted ``Notification``.
